_comment: Ordered reading lists returned by stellaris_learning_path. Each is a wiki page title to look up.

absolute-beginner.title: Absolute beginner - your first 50 years
absolute-beginner.audience: Never played / first game / confused by the UI

steps.why: Start here - the wiki's own onboarding walkthrough.
Learn what every panel on your screen is called, so we can talk about it.
The six resources and what each is actually for.
Pops are the engine of everything. Understand them and the rest follows.
Pops work jobs; jobs make resources. This is the core loop.
Districts create the jobs. Bigger planet = more districts.
Buildings refine what a planet is good at.
How to claim more planets without crashing your economy.
The tech tree basics and why research speed matters more than anything.
Exploring, anomalies and why you should survey everything.
Empire Size - the thing that punishes blind expansion.
Build a navy before someone else builds one for you.

economy.title: Economy - from red numbers to a working empire
economy.audience: You keep running out of consumer goods / energy / alloys

steps.why: The resource loop end to end.
Which jobs produce what, and their upkeep.
Specialising planets is the single biggest economy win.
Trade value, routes and piracy - the invisible economy.
Buying and selling without wrecking your prices.
Why your pops are unhappy even though they have jobs.
The multiplier that quietly decides every planet's output.
Ruler/specialist/worker balance and political weight.
Empire size: the cost of getting big.
Turning a pile of colonies into a real economy.

warfare.title: Warfare - fleets, ships and winning fights
warfare.audience: You want to fight, or you keep losing fights

steps.why: How war actually works: goals, occupation, exhaustion.
Fleet capacity, command limit and fleet management.
Designing ships instead of using auto-design.
Which weapons counter which defences.
Hull sizes, sections and what each hull is for.
The space-battle simulation: range, accuracy, evasion.
Bastions and FTL inhibitors - how to hold a chokepoint.
You still have to take the planet.
Why you did not get the system you just conquered.
Why you got forced into a Status Quo peace.
Outposts, borders and claiming systems.
Empire size and administrative efficiency.
Delegating planet management.
Making each planet good at one thing.
When and where to settle.
Why your new colony is underperforming.
Vassals as a way to grow without empire-size pain.

midgame.title: Mid-game - traditions, federations and ascension
midgame.audience: You have a stable empire and 100+ years in

steps.why: Which trees to take and in what order.
The permanent power spikes.
Psionic, cybernetic, synthetic, genetic - pick one.
Allies that actually matter.
The galactic senate and resolutions.
Intel and operations.
The long-term construction goals.
What the end-game crises are.
Ring worlds, dyson spheres, and how to afford them.
Fallen empires wake up.
You cannot beat a crisis alone.
Total war and planet-killing.
Where research goes when the tree is done.

gestalt.title: Gestalt empires (hive mind / machine intelligence)
gestalt.audience: Playing as a hive mind or robots

steps.why: The rules change completely.
Synapse drones, no consumer goods, no factions.
Pop assembly instead of growth.
Assembly vs. growth.
If you are a Rogue Servitor.
